title: Expected value, variance and standard deviation
objective: Given the probability distribution of a discrete random variable, calculate its expected value, variance and standard deviation.

blocks.text: The expected value of a discrete random variable X, also called the mean of its probability distribution, is the sum of each value multiplied by its probability. In the same way, the expectation of a function g(X) weights each g(xᵢ) by its probability.

blocks.tex: \mu = E(X) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} x_i\,P(X = x_i), \qquad E\big(g(X)\big) = \sum_{i=1}^{n} g(x_i)\,P(X = x_i)

blocks.text: The variance measures how far the values lie from the mean: it is the expected squared distance from the mean, which simplifies to the expectation of X² minus the square of the expectation of X.
The standard deviation is the square root of the variance.
For any numbers a and b: E(a) = a, E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b, E(X + Y) = E(X) + E(Y), Var(a) = 0 and Var(aX + b) = a²Var(X). Adding a constant moves the mean but does not change the spread.

blocks.tex: E(aX + b) = aE(X) + b, \qquad \operatorname{Var}(aX + b) = a^2\operatorname{Var}(X)

blocks.text: The probabilities of a probability distribution are never negative and add up to 1, which is how an unknown probability in a table is found.
